quranic_mention: Named across more than a dozen surahs; the fullest accounts are in Hud, al-Hijr, ash-Shu'ara and al-'Ankabut
teaser: One believing household in an entire city. When the angels came, they found no other — and the town was turned over onto itself before sunrise had finished.

layers.title: Who
layers.subtitle: Ibrahim's nephew, and the first man in the Quran recorded as believing him.
layers.source: Ibn Kathir, Stories of the Prophets
layers.content:
Lut, peace be upon him, is introduced in the Quran by an act of faith in someone else: «فَآمَنَ لَهُ لُوطٌ» — "And Lut believed him." (Quran 29:26) The one believed is Ibrahim. Ibn Kathir records from the genealogists that Lut was the son of Haran, Ibrahim's brother — a nephew, and among the very first to accept what his uncle brought.

He emigrated with him: «وَنَجَّيْنَاهُ وَلُوطًا إِلَى الْأَرْضِ الَّتِي بَارَكْنَا فِيهَا لِلْعَالَمِينَ» — "And We delivered him and Lut to the land which We had blessed for the worlds." (Quran 21:71) Then Allah made him a prophet with an assignment of his own: «وَلُوطًا آتَيْنَاهُ حُكْمًا وَعِلْمًا» — "And to Lut We gave judgement and knowledge." (Quran 21:74)

Ibn Kathir places the towns he was sent to — Sadum and its neighbours — on the western side of the Dead Sea, after Ibrahim's departure from Egypt. The Quran itself does not name the city. It describes it instead: «الْقَرْيَةِ الَّتِي كَانَت تَّعْمَلُ الْخَبَائِثَ» — "the city that was committing wicked deeds." (Quran 21:74) And it fixes the ruins on a road people still travel: «وَإِنَّهَا لَبِسَبِيلٍ مُّقِيمٍ» — "and indeed, it is on an established road." (Quran 15:76)

The Quran gives their character in one verse of three charges: «إِنَّكُمْ لَتَأْتُونَ الرِّجَالَ وَتَقْطَعُونَ السَّبِيلَ وَتَأْتُونَ فِي نَادِيكُمُ الْمُنكَرَ» — you approach men, you cut off the road, and you commit indecency in your gatherings (Quran 29:29). Ibn Kathir explains the middle charge as highway robbery of travellers. The last is the worst detail: not sin in the dark, but sin in the assembly.

layers.title: The Call
layers.subtitle: A sin no nation had committed before — and a town that answered by exiling purity.
layers.source: Ibn Kathir, Stories of the Prophets
layers.content:
«أَتَأْتُونَ الْفَاحِشَةَ مَا سَبَقَكُم بِهَا مِنْ أَحَدٍ مِّنَ الْعَالَمِينَ» — "Do you commit such immorality as no one has preceded you with among the worlds?" (Quran 7:80) Ibn Kathir stops on that clause: they were the inventors. Before this town, no people on earth had done it.

In Surah ash-Shu'ara his call opens the way every prophet's does — will you not fear Allah, I am a trustworthy messenger to you, I ask no reward (Quran 26:161-164) — and then narrows to the specific: «أَتَأْتُونَ الذُّكْرَانَ مِنَ الْعَالَمِينَ • وَتَذَرُونَ مَا خَلَقَ لَكُمْ رَبُّكُم مِّنْ أَزْوَاجِكُم» — "Do you approach males among the worlds, and leave what your Lord has created for you as mates?" (Quran 26:165-166) The argument is not disgust. It is that something was created for them and they walked past it.

Their reply is one of the most chilling sentences in the Quran: «أَخْرِجُوهُم مِّن قَرْيَتِكُمْ إِنَّهُمْ أُنَاسٌ يَتَطَهَّرُونَ» — "Expel them from your city! Indeed, they are people who keep themselves pure." (Quran 7:82) The stated ground for banishment is that Lut and his household were clean. Purity had become the offence.

And to him directly: «لَئِن لَّمْ تَنتَهِ يَا لُوطُ لَتَكُونَنَّ مِنَ الْمُخْرَجِينَ» — "If you do not desist, O Lut, you will surely be of those evicted." (Quran 26:167) Ibn Kathir notes he preached for years and no one outside his own family answered him.

layers.title: The Trial
layers.subtitle: A mob at his door, guests he could not protect, and a wife who informed on him.
layers.source: Ibn Kathir, Stories of the Prophets
layers.content:
The angels came to him as young men, and Lut understood immediately what his own town would do to guests: «سِيءَ بِهِمْ وَضَاقَ بِهِمْ ذَرْعًا وَقَالَ هَذَا يَوْمٌ عَصِيبٌ» — "He was distressed for them and felt for them great uneasiness, and said: This is a trying day." (Quran 11:77)

The crowd arrived. He stood at the door and offered them lawful marriage instead: «هَؤُلَاءِ بَنَاتِي هُنَّ أَطْهَرُ لَكُمْ» — "These are my daughters; they are purer for you." (Quran 11:78) They answered: «مَا لَنَا فِي بَنَاتِكَ مِنْ حَقٍّ» — "We have no right to your daughters." (Quran 11:79) Of that moment Allah says: «لَعَمْرُكَ إِنَّهُمْ لَفِي سَكْرَتِهِمْ يَعْمَهُونَ» — "By your life, they were in their intoxication, wandering blindly." (Quran 15:72)

Then a prophet's breaking point, preserved in the Book: «لَوْ أَنَّ لِي بِكُمْ قُوَّةً أَوْ آوِي إِلَىٰ رُكْنٍ شَدِيدٍ» — "If only I had against you some power, or could take refuge in a strong support." (Quran 11:80) The Prophet ﷺ commented on this line with mercy rather than correction: "May Allah have mercy on Lut — he was already taking refuge in a mighty support." (Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of the Stories of the Prophets, narrated by Abu Hurayrah)

And the wound inside the house. His wife was not with him. «ضَرَبَ اللَّهُ مَثَلًا لِّلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا امْرَأَتَ نُوحٍ وَامْرَأَتَ لُوطٍ كَانَتَا تَحْتَ عَبْدَيْنِ مِنْ عِبَادِنَا صَالِحَيْنِ فَخَانَتَاهُمَا» — the wife of Nuh and the wife of Lut were under two righteous servants of Ours, and they both betrayed them (Quran 66:10). His two duas from those years survive: «رَبِّ نَجِّنِي وَأَهْلِي مِمَّا يَعْمَلُونَ» (Quran 26:169) and «رَبِّ انصُرْنِي عَلَى الْقَوْمِ الْمُفْسِدِينَ» (Quran 29:30).
layers.hadith_ref: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of the Stories of the Prophets — narrated by Abu Hurayrah

layers.title: The Sign
layers.subtitle: Eyes wiped blank, a city inverted, and one house counted in the whole town.
layers.source: Ibn Kathir, Stories of the Prophets
layers.content:
The angels ended his helplessness with a sentence: they were messengers, and the mob would not reach him. Then came the order to move: «فَأَسْرِ بِأَهْلِكَ بِقِطْعٍ مِّنَ اللَّيْلِ وَلَا يَلْتَفِتْ مِنكُمْ أَحَدٌ إِلَّا امْرَأَتَكَ» — "So set out with your family during a portion of the night, and let not any among you look back — except your wife." (Quran 11:81) The exception is stated as a decree, not a suspicion.

On the crowd outside, the first blow fell before dawn: «فَطَمَسْنَا أَعْيُنَهُمْ» — "and We blinded their eyes." (Quran 54:37) Then the town itself: «فَأَخَذَتْهُمُ الصَّيْحَةُ مُشْرِقِينَ» — "So the cry seized them at sunrise." (Quran 15:73) And: «جَعَلْنَا عَالِيَهَا سَافِلَهَا وَأَمْطَرْنَا عَلَيْهَا حِجَارَةً مِّن سِجِّيلٍ مَّنضُودٍ» — "We made its highest part its lowest, and rained upon them stones of layered hard clay." (Quran 11:82) The stones were «مُّسَوَّمَةً عِندَ رَبِّكَ» — marked from your Lord (Quran 11:83). Nothing about it was random.

But the verse that should stay with the reader is the census. Surah adh-Dhariyat records what the angels found when they went in to save the believers: «فَمَا وَجَدْنَا فِيهَا غَيْرَ بَيْتٍ مِّنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ» — "And We found not within it other than a single house of Muslims." (Quran 51:36)

One house. Not one street, not one minority quarter. Lut had preached for years to a whole city and the final count was his own household — and even that not complete. The sign of Lut is not a staff or a fire. It is a city turned upside down, and a man who kept calling anyway when the arithmetic had long stopped working in his favour.

layers.title: The Legacy
layers.subtitle: Nearness to a prophet saved no one. Standing alone saved a household.
layers.source: Ibn Kathir, Stories of the Prophets
layers.content:
Allah's verdict on him: «وَأَدْخَلْنَاهُ فِي رَحْمَتِنَا إِنَّهُ مِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ» — "And We admitted him into Our mercy; indeed, he was of the righteous." (Quran 21:75) In Surah al-An'am he is listed among the prophets Allah favoured above the worlds (Quran 6:86). He is one of very few prophets whose entire recorded mission produced no community of followers, and Allah still calls it success.

The second inheritance is his wife, and it is the reason Allah cites her by name in a surah revealed centuries later. She shared his home, his table, and his name, and she is used in the Quran as the standing example for disbelievers (Quran 66:10). Ibn Kathir draws the plain conclusion: lineage and proximity transmit nothing. A prophet could not save his own wife; a wife could not be saved by her prophet.

The third is a warning still sitting on a map. «وَتَرَكْنَا فِيهَا آيَةً لِّلَّذِينَ يَخَافُونَ الْعَذَابَ الْأَلِيمَ» — "And We left therein a sign for those who fear the painful punishment." (Quran 51:37) And it was deliberately placed where caravans pass: «وَإِنَّهَا لَبِسَبِيلٍ مُّقِيمٍ» (Quran 15:76). Ibn Kathir observes that the act itself came to carry the town's name — the shame outlived the city.

What Lut leaves the believer is a hard, useful mathematics. His people were not destroyed for a sin done in private; they were destroyed for a sin normalised in public, defended socially, and finally used as grounds to exile the people who abstained. When purity becomes the thing a society finds offensive, the Quran has already told us what stage that society has reached.

quiz.prompt: What is Lut's first recorded act in the Quran?

options.text: He destroyed the idols of his town
He believed in Ibrahim
He built a house of worship
He led an army against Sodom

quiz.scholar_reflection: Ibn Kathir identifies him as Ibrahim's nephew, son of his brother Haran, and among the first to accept his message. His prophethood began as someone else's follower.

quiz.prompt: In Quran 29:29, Lut names three habits of his people. What are they?

options.text: Idol worship, cheating in trade, and infanticide
Approaching men, robbing travellers on the road, and committing indecency openly in their gatherings
Magic, gambling, and drinking
Refusing charity, breaking oaths, and burning crops

quiz.citation: Quran 29:29 — «إِنَّكُمْ لَتَأْتُونَ الرِّجَالَ وَتَقْطَعُونَ السَّبِيلَ وَتَأْتُونَ فِي نَادِيكُمُ الْمُنكَرَ»
quiz.scholar_reflection: Ibn Kathir reads the middle charge as highway robbery of travellers. The third is the most revealing: the sin had moved out of private rooms and into the public assembly.

quiz.prompt: What reason did the people of the city give for wanting to expel Lut and his household?

options.text: That he was a foreigner and owned no land
That he had insulted their ancestors
That they were people who kept themselves pure
That he refused to pay their tax

quiz.citation: Quran 7:82 — «أَخْرِجُوهُم مِّن قَرْيَتِكُمْ إِنَّهُمْ أُنَاسٌ يَتَطَهَّرُونَ»
quiz.scholar_reflection: They stated the accusation as though it were self-evidently damning. A society can reach a point where abstaining is read as an attack on everyone else.

quiz.prompt: When the angels went into the city to remove the believers, how many believing households did they find?

options.text: Seventy households
A single house
Half the town
None at all

quiz.citation: Quran 51:36 — «فَمَا وَجَدْنَا فِيهَا غَيْرَ بَيْتٍ مِّنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ»
quiz.scholar_reflection: Years of calling, and the final tally was his own household — and his wife was not counted in it. Allah still records his mission as entry into His mercy (Quran 21:75).

quiz.prompt: How does the Quran describe the end of the city?

options.text: It was swallowed by the sea
Its people were blinded, then a cry seized them at sunrise, and the city was turned upside down with marked stones of hard clay
A wind carried it away over seven nights
It was besieged and starved

quiz.scholar_reflection: Even the stones are described as «مُّسَوَّمَةً عِندَ رَبِّكَ» — marked from your Lord. The punishment was as precisely targeted as the warning had been.

quiz.prompt: Lut's people committed their sin «فِي نَادِيكُمُ» — in the open assembly. What has become normal in your own surroundings that you would once have found unthinkable?

options.text: Something in how people speak about others
Something in what I watch or scroll past without flinching
Something in how money is earned around me
I cannot name one, which may mean my own baseline has already moved

quiz.scholar_reflection: The Quran treats openness as an aggravation, not a detail. Sin that has stopped needing to hide has already changed the people who watch it.
quiz.slider_label: How much has your baseline shifted?

quiz.prompt: His wife shared his house and was not saved. Which relationship are you quietly counting on to carry you spiritually?

options.text: A religious parent or grandparent whose reputation I inherit
A practising spouse whose routine I lean on
A community or teacher I am associated with
None — and that leaves me with no cover at all

quiz.citation: Quran 66:10 — the wife of Nuh and the wife of Lut
quiz.scholar_reflection: Allah chose two prophets' wives as the standing example for disbelievers. Proximity to guidance is not the same as accepting it, and the Quran refuses to let the two be confused.
quiz.slider_label: How much of your deen is borrowed?

quiz.prompt: "If only I had against you some power." When you are outnumbered and cannot enforce what is right, what do you actually do?

options.text: I get louder, then exhausted, then silent
I withdraw and protect my own household only
I keep speaking without expecting to be heard
I tell myself I am waiting for a better moment

quiz.citation: Quran 11:80; Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of the Stories of the Prophets
quiz.scholar_reflection: The Prophet ﷺ answered Lut's cry not with rebuke but with mercy, noting that he was already taking refuge in a mighty support. Feeling powerless is not the same as being abandoned.
quiz.slider_label: Where do you turn when you have no leverage?

quiz.prompt: Allah counted one believing house in an entire city and called Lut's mission a success. How do you measure whether your own effort in the deen is working?

options.text: By whether anyone visibly changes because of me
By whether I am respected for it
By whether I kept doing it when nothing changed
Honestly, I stop measuring once results dry up

quiz.scholar_reflection: Ibn Kathir does not soften the outcome: no community followed him. Allah then says He admitted Lut into His mercy. Results were never the metric being recorded.

quiz.prompt: «وَلَا يَلْتَفِتْ مِنكُمْ أَحَدٌ» — do not look back. What are you still looking back at when you try to leave something behind?

options.text: A habit I left but still visit in my imagination
People I had to distance myself from
A version of myself I secretly miss
A comfort I gave up and have not stopped resenting the loss of

quiz.scholar_reflection: The instruction was not cruelty. Leaving a place of ruin requires the eyes to commit as fully as the feet, or the body arrives somewhere the heart never left.
quiz.slider_label: How completely have you actually left?
